introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: ANSWER ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: ANSWER ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the letters from the table, select an element that is

(i) Stored in paraffin oil.

(ii) A reddish liquid at RTP. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Position of the elements: the table has four periods. A is in Group I, period 2 (lithium); B is in Group II, period 3 (magnesium); E is in Group III, period 3 (aluminium); F and G are in Group VII, periods 2 and 3; H is in Group 0, period 1.

(i) **A.** It is a Group I (alkali) metal. These metals react quickly with oxygen and moisture in the air, so they are stored under paraffin oil.

(ii) The reddish-brown liquid at room temperature and pressure is **bromine**, a Group VII element (halogen). On this table bromine would occupy the cell directly below G (period 4), and that cell carries no letter. The closest letter is therefore **G**, the halogen in the same group (F and G are the only halogens shown). *Note: the question is imprecise; see the uncertainty note.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
Write the electronic configuration of:

(i) B:

(ii) Why is B classified in group II? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
B is in period 3 and Group II (the same row as E), so it is magnesium with 12 electrons.

(i) Electronic configuration of B: **2, 8, 2**.

(ii) B has **2 electrons in its outermost shell**, and the group number of a main-group element equals the number of outer-shell electrons, so it is placed in Group II.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The element, E, has a relative atomic mass of 27. Give the composition of an atom of E.

(i) Number of protons:

(ii) Number of electrons:

(iii) Number of neutrons: *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
E is in Group III, period 3, so it is aluminium. Its atomic number is $2 + 8 + 3 = 13$.

(i) Number of protons = atomic number = **13**.

(ii) An atom is neutral, so number of electrons = **13**.

(iii) Number of neutrons = mass number $-$ number of protons $= 27 - 13 =$ **14**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two elements X and Y have atomic numbers of 6 and 17 respectively.

(i) Write the formula of the compound formed between X and Y.

(ii) Identify the bond type in the compound in d(i) above.
questions.corrige_markdown:
X has atomic number 6, electronic configuration 2, 4 (carbon): it needs 4 more electrons. Y has atomic number 17, configuration 2, 8, 7 (chlorine): it needs 1 more electron.

(i) One carbon atom shares one electron with each of four chlorine atoms: formula $\mathrm{CCl_4}$.

(ii) The bond is **covalent**: both elements are non-metals and they share electrons in pairs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Sodium chloride has the formula NaCl.

Identify the charge of the metallic ion: *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Sodium (2, 8, 1) loses its one outer electron to form the ion $\mathrm{Na^+}$. The charge is **+1**. The compound is neutral because the chloride ion $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ carries a charge of $-1$.
